title: Hexagon lace shawl
subtitle: Geometric hexagon motifs joined into a crescent shawl.
excerpt: Individual hexagon motifs in fingering weight are joined as you go into a crescent shape. The open mesh between motifs keeps the fabric airy and the geometric lines give it a modern edge.
sourceNotes: Hexagon motif construction draws on traditional Continental European hexagon lace traditions documented in 19th-century pattern books (Weldon's Practical Crochet series, Internet Archive). Crescent shaping and JAYG method are modern interpretations.

glossaryTerms.definition: A six-sided flat crochet piece worked in the round, beginning from a centre ring and built up in rounds of clusters and chain spaces to form six equal points.
Attaching a new motif to completed neighbours during its final round by replacing chain arches with slip stitches into matching arches on adjacent motifs.
The gap formed by one or more chains that the next round works into rather than into individual stitches.
Wetting or steaming finished crochet and pinning it to the stated dimensions so the lace opens up and the fabric holds its shape when dry.

crochet.finishedSizeText: Crescent shawl, 160 cm wingspan x 45 cm deep at centre back, blocked.

content.text: A hexagon lace shawl is built from individual
hexagon motifs
that are
joined as you go
into a crescent shape. Each motif is 8 cm point to point after
blocking
. The finished shawl is 160 cm across the wingspan and 45 cm deep at the centre back.

The motifs are arranged in rows that increase by one hexagon on each row until the widest point is reached. Flat-joining keeps the surface smooth on both sides. The gaps between the motifs become part of the design, creating a lattice of open
chain spaces
across the whole piece.
What you need

items.name: Fingering weight yarn
items.substitutions: Any smooth lace or fingering yarn in natural or plant fibre blocks well.

content.text: Gauge

One hexagon motif = 8 cm point to point with a 3.5 mm hook in fingering yarn, blocked. Work one motif and block it before starting the full shawl. If your motif is wider than 8 cm, go down one hook size. If narrower, go up. The crescent shaping depends on accurate motif size to stay flat.
Stitches used
ch: chain
sl st: slip stitch
dc (UK): double crochet, insert hook, pull through, two loops off together
tr (UK): treble, one yarn-over before inserting, three loops worked off two at a time
Single hexagon motif
Foundation ring: ch 6, sl st to first ch to form a ring.
Round 1: Ch 3 (counts as 1 tr). Work 2 tr into ring, ch 2. *3 tr into ring, ch 2*. Repeat 5 more times. Sl st to top of ch-3 to close. (6 clusters, 6 ch-2 corner spaces.)

Round 2: Sl st into first ch-2 corner space. Ch 3. Work (2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr) into same space. Ch 1. *(3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr) into next corner, ch 1*. Repeat around. Sl st to close. (12 clusters, 6 ch-2 points, 6 ch-1 sides.)

Round 3: Sl st to corner. Ch 3. Work (2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr) into corner. *(Ch 1, 3 tr into ch-1 side space, ch 1, (3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr) into next corner)*. Repeat around. Sl st. Fasten off. (18 clusters, 6 points, 12 sides.)
Crescent arrangement
The shawl is built in diagonal rows with the flat edge of the crescent at the top.
Row 1: Work 1 motif. Fasten off.
Row 2: Work 2 motifs side by side. On the second motif's Round 3,
join as you go
to the first along one shared side: replace the ch-2 point with ch 1, sl st into matching point of adjacent motif, ch 1. Fasten off.

Continue adding one more motif per row. Each new row joins to the row above along the top points. Stagger the motifs so each one sits in the gap between two motifs in the row above, like a brick course. Work 9 rows total to reach the 160 cm wingspan.
Finishing

Weave in all tails with the tapestry needle. Block the finished shawl by soaking in cool water for 20 minutes, pressing out excess water in a towel, and pinning each hexagon point to the blocking mat at the stated dimensions. Leave to dry fully before removing pins.
Blocking
opens the chain spaces and makes the points sharp.

attrs.heading: Common problems
attrs.intro: Hexagon join shawls have a few predictable trouble spots.

items.cause: Motifs not blocked before joining or tension too tight
items.fix: Block every completed row before adding the next, or at minimum block the finished piece aggressively by pinning out each hexagon point.

items.cause: Inconsistent tension on the joining round
items.fix: Work the joining sl sts loosely; hold the two motifs face to face and ease the hook through both loops.
Check that each new row has exactly one more motif than the row above and that the joins are staggered, not lined up in straight columns.
